findings.title: All game-server traffic (highscore + achievements cookie) sent over plain HTTP
findings.code_excerpt:
public final static String HIGHSCORE_GETPHP = "http://www.apo-games.de/apoIcarus/get_highscore.php";
public final static String HIGHSCORE_SAVEPHP = "http://www.apo-games.de/apoIcarus/save_highscore.php";
findings.entry_point: Player selects 'highscore' menu or finishes a run; also applet achievement sync. Endpoints hard-coded at ApoConstants.java:24-25 and apoJump/ApoJumpConstants.java:8 (PROGRAM_URL).
findings.sink: url.openConnection() in ApoHighscore.save/load (org/apogames/help/ApoHighscore.java:63 and :109) and ApoHelp.saveData/loadData (org/apogames/help/ApoHelp.java:424 and :452, 'cookies.php')
findings.data_path: ApoJumpStateGame.upload() -> ApoHighscore.save() -> new URL(HIGHSCORE_SAVEPHP).openConnection(); ApoJumpPanel.init():75 -> ApoJumpStateAchievements.loadAchievements():64 -> ApoHelp.loadData(new URL(PROGRAM_URL), COOKIE_NAME) -> cookies.php over http://.
findings.attack_scenario: 1) Attacker on the same LAN/DNS path passively sniffs port 80: sees player-submitted names, points, times, and the achievements-cookie values of every client. 2) Active MITM rewrites responses (see findings 03/04) or the save request itself. No TLS or pinning exists anywhere in the variant to stop this.
findings.preconditions: ApoConstants.B_ONLINE is hard-coded true (ApoConstants.java:16); attacker needs a network vantage point (same LAN, ARP/DNS spoof, rogue DHCP) or control of apo-games.de resolution.
findings.validation_plan: Point www.apo-games.de to a local listener via /etc/hosts, start ApoJumpMain, open the highscore screen and finish one run. Observer shows cleartext POST bodies 'points=..&time=..&name=..' and 'GET=&name=apoIcarus_level' / 'SET=&name=..' to /apoIcarus/cookies.php. tcpdump/wireshark confirms zero TLS handshake.

findings.title: Highscore submission is unsigned and unauthenticated: leaderboard fully forgeable by local user
findings.entry_point: The server accepts these POSTs from anyone; the only sender-side gate is the in-game flow ApoJumpStateGame.uploadScore() -> upload() (apoJump/game/ApoJumpStateGame.java:211-219), which carries no session token, signature, or proof-of-play.
findings.sink: printout.writeBytes(content) at ApoHighscore.java:77 into the POST to save_highscore.php
findings.data_path: Game-computed points/time come from ApoJumpLevel.getPoints()/getTime(), name from an 11-char textfield, but none of it is bound to any credential: the wire format is exactly three form fields, so the same request can be produced outside the game with arbitrary values.
findings.attack_scenario: A cheater runs: curl -X POST -d 'points=999999999&time=0&name=<anyone>' http://www.apo-games.de/apoIcarus/save_highscore.php --data-urlencode nothing else required. Next client that opens the highscore list displays the forged score at rank 1 (rendered in ApoJumpStateHighscore.render:215-228), and ApoJumpLevel draws the fake leader's name in-game (level render lines 428-434). Attacker gains leaderboard defacement / impersonation of other players' names.
findings.preconditions: save_highscore.php reachable and still accepting submissions (no client-side check beyond B_ONLINE=true).
findings.validation_plan: Replay the exact byte sequence the client sends (capture per finding 01) with modified points/name via curl/netcat. Re-open the highscore menu in the game and observe the forged entry sorted first by ApoJumpStateHighscore.sortList().

findings.title: Achievements stored server-side via cookies.php and trusted blindly on load (applet mode)
findings.entry_point: Server response line from codebase+'cookies.php' (plain HTTP), returned to apoJump/game/ApoJumpStateAchievements.java:64 loadAchievements(), which treats every digit character as an earned-achievement index.
findings.sink: this.addAchievements(ACHIEVEMENTS_ARRAY[value], false) at ApoJumpStateAchievements.java:77, fed by ApoHelp.loadData()'s unauthenticated readLine() result (ApoHelp.java:465)
findings.data_path: HTTP response string -> loadAchievements() char loop (lines 71-84): each char Integer.valueOf'd, guarded only by value < ACHIEVEMENTS_ARRAY.length -> addAchievements(). Write side equally unauthenticated: saveAchievements() (line 97) POSTs 'SET=&name=apoIcarus_level&value=<digits>'. No user identity binds the cookie row, so any writer owns every profile.
findings.attack_scenario: MITM (or anyone issuing a direct request) sends SET=&name=apoIcarus_level&value=01234567 to cookies.php; every subsequent client loading achievements for that cookie value sees all 8 achievements unlocked. Conversely a MITM can strip/tamper stored progress. Gained: trivial achievement forgery and cross-user tampering on the shared service.
findings.preconditions: Only active when ApoConstants.B_APPLET == true (set in apoJump/ApoJumpApplet.java:26 / ApoScreen.initApplet:159) - i.e., web-applet deployments; desktop runs skip both paths. Requires reachability of the HTTP endpoint or a MITM position.
findings.validation_plan: Run the applet variant against a local rehost of PROGRAM_URL serving a stub cookies.php that answers GET=&name=apoIcarus_level with '0134'. Achievements screen lists indices 0,1,3,4 as earned. Then issue the raw SET request yourself and reload to confirm overwrite.

findings.title: Uncaught IndexOutOfBounds on death when highscore list has fewer than 2 entries: remote crash of game thread
findings.entry_point: Shape of the get_highscore.php response: ApoHighscore.load() builds points/time/names lists purely from response lines (org/apogames/help/ApoHighscore.java:129-138); sortList() copies them into help (apoJump/game/ApoJumpStateHighscore.java:106-124). A malicious/MITM server (or simply a dead endpoint - load failure leaves help empty) controls help.size().
findings.sink: List.get(1) with size<2 inside isFirstPosition(), reached on every player death via setWin() <- ApoJumpPlayer.think() (apoJump/entity/ApoJumpPlayer.java:109-110); exception propagates uncached through ApoJumpLevel.think:324 -> ApoJumpStateGame.think:235 -> ApoJumpPanel.think:212 -> ApoSubGame.run think call (org/apogames/ApoSubGame.java:110), killing the game thread.
findings.data_path: HTTP response (0 or 3 lines = 0/1 entries) -> ApoHighscore.load() -> ApoJumpStateHighscore.sortList() -> help list of size<2 -> player dies -> ApoJumpLevel.setWin():301 calls isFirstPosition():308 -> get(1) throws IndexOutOfBoundsException -> no try/catch anywhere up the think chain -> thread dies, frame freezes.
findings.attack_scenario: Attacker who can answer the client's HTTP request returns e.g. a single entry ('100\n50\nAlice'). The victim plays until their inevitable first death; instead of the game-over dialog, an unhandled IndexOutOfBoundsException kills the game loop and the window hangs. Same crash occurs benignly whenever the online highscore cannot be fetched. Attacker gains reliable denial of the running session; no persistence or code execution.
findings.preconditions: B_ONLINE=true (always, desktop included); server response yields fewer than 2 entries either via attack or outage. Note the sibling parse error path (non-multiple-of-3 line counts) IS caught in ApoJumpStateHighscore.load():75-84 - only this consumer is unguarded.
findings.validation_plan: Rehost the endpoints (hosts file): stub get_highscore.php to return exactly '100\n50\nAlice'. Play until death. Observe stack trace IndexOutOfBoundsException at ApoJumpLevel.isFirstPosition and a frozen, non-responsive game frame. Control: return two entries and death proceeds normally.

findings.title: Unbounded parse of highscore response: malicious server can exhaust client heap
findings.entry_point: Response stream of get_highscore.php opened at ApoHighscore.java:109-126; triggered whenever the highscore state initializes (ApoJumpStateHighscore.init:43) or after each upload (ApoJumpStateGame.upload:221).
findings.sink: ArrayList.add(String) in the readLine loop (names.add at :135) with no cap on iteration count or line length
findings.data_path: Malicious/MITM server keeps the connection open and streams valid integer pairs plus arbitrarily many/long name lines -> each becomes a retained String in three ArrayLists -> heap growth until OOM. Client offers no limit, timeout, or Content-Length check.
findings.attack_scenario: Attacker controlling the endpoint (or MITM with a slow-drip stream) answers a highscore fetch with gigabytes of '0\n0\nAAAA...' lines; the EDT-independent loader thread allocates until OutOfMemoryError. Gained: client freeze/crash during normal play; combined with finding 01 requires only network position.
findings.preconditions: Network control of the endpoint response; game must perform a highscore load (automatic on menu use and post-upload).
findings.validation_plan:
Stub server script streams '1
1
x
' repeated ~10^7 times slowly. Run game, open highscore screen, watch RSS/jconsole heap climb until OutOfMemoryError in ApoHighscore.load. Compare with a 10-entry response (flat memory).

findings.title: URLClassLoader-based remote/local class instantiation present but dead in this variant
findings.entry_point: None in this variant: grep across all 59 files finds zero instantiations of ApoClassLoader and zero external references (only its own definition). Constructor takes arbitrary path + classname; path becomes File URI (desktop) or raw URL (applet) per lines 65-68.
findings.sink: Class.newInstance() at ApoClassLoader.java:75 executing attacker-supplied bytecode's constructor/static initializer
findings.data_path: Theoretical: caller-provided (path, classname) -> getMyClass() -> URLClassLoader over that location -> loadClass -> newInstance. No current data flow reaches it because no caller exists; the risk materializes only if sibling variants wired level/editor or update logic to it with externally influenced arguments.
findings.attack_scenario: Latent only: if a clone-and-own sibling passes an attacker-influenced path/classname (e.g., a downloaded 'level pack' directory), pointing it at hostile .class bytes yields immediate code execution in-process. In ApoIcarus as shipped, an attacker has no route to this sink.
findings.preconditions: Requires code changes (a caller supplying attacker-controlled path/classname); not exploitable in this variant as-is.
findings.validation_plan: (1) Confirm deadness: grep -rn 'ApoClassLoader' returns only org/apogames/help/ApoClassLoader.java. (2) Prove impact-if-wired: compile class Evil{ public Evil(){Runtime.getRuntime().exec("calc")}} into /tmp/evil/, then invoke new ApoClassLoader("file:/tmp/evil/","Evil").getMyClass() from any test main - constructor executes.

findings.title: MD5 helper (getMd5Digest) shipped but never called in this variant
findings.entry_point: None: grep over the whole tree shows the single reference is the definition itself (ApoHelp.java:301). No validation/highscore logic invokes it here, unlike some sibling variants where MD5 guards score submission.
findings.sink: MD5 digest computation; would matter only if used for integrity/authentication, which currently it is not
findings.data_path: No data reaches this method in ApoIcarus; it is cloned shared infrastructure awaiting reuse. Reported as theoretical so corpus-wide propagation studies can distinguish 'flawed primitive present' from 'flawed primitive reachable'.
findings.attack_scenario: None in this variant. If a future/sibling caller uses it to sign highscores (the pattern seen elsewhere in the corpus), forged-score attacks reduce to MD5 collision/preimage work or simple hash replay.
findings.preconditions: A caller must be added (or inherited via clone-and-own) before any attacker interaction is possible.
findings.validation_plan: grep -rn 'getMd5Digest' across the variant returns only the definition - proves absence of reachability. Cross-check sibling variants' callers to confirm the shared-component hypothesis about where it does become live.

categories_checked_and_absent: untrusted_deserialization - no java.io.ObjectInputStream/readObject anywhere (grep over all files)

path_traversal - no user-editable save/level/replay files exist in this variant (levels are procedural, ApoJumpLevel.makePlatforms); the only File-based helpers (ApoIO.readLevel/writeLevel, ApoCopy, ApoImageScale, ApoImage.getPic(bLoad=true)) have zero callers, and all actual image loads are JAR resources with literal paths
credential_or_secret_exposure - no passwords/tokens/API keys in source
legacy_sandbox_assumption - no SecurityManager/doPrivileged code; applet mode merely flips B_APPLET for the HTTP cookie store
information_disclosure - beyond plaintext transport of submitted name/score (covered by finding 01), nothing sensitive is logged or persisted locally
notes: Source tree is nested under Users/eliahilse/Documents/GitHub/B/apogames/Java/ApoIcarus inside the provided root (59 .java files, no resources). This is the smallest attack surface in the corpus family: levels are generated procedurally (apoJump/level/ApoJumpLevel.makePlatforms), there are NO .cheat/.mar/.skunk/.defence/.rep-style files, no ObjectInputStream, and no defineClass. The entire untrusted-input surface is the plain-HTTP channel to apo-games.de: highscore GET/SAVE (ApoHighscore) and the achievements cookie store (ApoHelp.saveData/loadData, applet-only), which explains why findings cluster on insecure_transport/client_side_trust. Desktop entry point ApoJumpMain.main ignores argv entirely. Cloned-but-dead infrastructure found unused here: ApoClassLoader, ApoIO (+ its abstract level format), ApoCopy, ApoFileFilter/ApoFileNameFilter, ApoSplashScreen, ApoImageScale, RawScale2x/3x, and ApoHelp.getMd5Digest - valuable markers for measuring flaw propagation in sibling variants. Minor non-security robustness notes: ApoHelp.saveData/loadData send a body with setRequestMethod(GET) and do not URL-encode name/value (safe with today's constant/digit-only values); clipboard paste into the name field is bounded (maxLength 11, printable ASCII 33-126, ApoNewTextfield.addCharacter:295-302); ApoJumpLevel.isFirstPosition assumes >=2 highscore entries (finding 04). All remote findings additionally depend on the apo-games.de endpoints being resolvable/alive or an attacker redirecting them (hosts/DNS), since URLs are hard-coded.
